assistantMessageEvent.content: JSON Lines (JSONL), also called newline-delimited JSON, emerged in the early 2010s as a pragmatic format for streaming structured data. While JSON itself was popularized by Douglas Crockford in the early 2000s, its standard form wasn't suited to logs or record streams, since parsing required loading an entire document. By placing one valid JSON object per line, each record became independently parseable, enabling append-only writes and incremental reads. The format gained traction through tools like Graylog, Elasticsearch's bulk API, and data pipelines, and was formally specified by Ian Ward around 2015 at jsonlines.org. Today it remains a de facto standard for logs, datasets, and LLM training data.
